Chapter 6: Making Choices—Deciding with Confidence and Letting Go.
So, after exploring your options and trying out a few prototypes, you hit the next big hurdle—actually making a decision. Sound familiar? A lot of us freeze at this stage, worrying about making the wrong move or regretting our choice later.
But what if we flipped the script? Instead of treating decisions like a pass-or-fail test, imagine them as a creative act. There isn’t just one “correct” answer. The goal isn’t perfect certainty—it’s about making a good choice with what you know right now, and then really committing to it.
Here’s something to keep in mind: No decision can promise a flawless outcome. Every path comes with its own set of trade-offs. Waiting around for absolute clarity? That’ll just keep you stuck.
Think of it like crossing a river, stepping from stone to stone. You can only see the next step as you move forward. Standing in place, hoping for everything to line up perfectly, won’t get you across.
So, how do you actually decide with confidence? Let’s break down a few techniques that really help:
First, gather and weigh your information. Look back at what you discovered from prototyping, chatting with others, and your own reflections. Which options light you up? Which ones line up with what matters most to you?
Next, try to discern between your choices. Instead of endlessly comparing every detail, focus on your compass—what’s truly important to you? Sometimes, jotting down a simple pros and cons list can make your feelings much clearer.
Once you’re ready, go ahead and make the choice. Mark the moment—maybe tell a friend, write it down, or take one small, real step in that direction.
And here’s a big one: Let go of the alternatives. After you choose, consciously release the other options. This stops you from getting bogged down by “what ifs” or feeling like you’re missing out.
For example, imagine someone who’s tested out a few different career paths and finally decides to become a teacher. Sure, there might be trade-offs, like less pay. But there’s a deeper sense of meaning. Instead of second-guessing, they commit fully to that path.
There’s also something called “decision coherence.” Basically, it’s about making sure your choice fits with your gut and your values—not just what others expect from you. If it feels right deep down and lines up with your vision for life and work, you’re probably on a good track—even if it isn’t perfect.
And remember, most decisions aren’t set in stone. Life design is all about experimenting, learning, and adjusting. If something doesn’t work out, you can always circle back, brainstorm new ideas, and try again.
The real key? Keep moving forward. Keep learning. And trust yourself to make choices with confidence—and let go of the rest.
